title: Mapping endogenous steering resistance: which concepts do small models fight back on?

original_idea.body: On a small model with an available SAE, measure realized-vs-intended steering shift as a resistance gap per safety concept and surface candidate SAE resistance features.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible reliability-of-control chain, but the link to a concrete catastrophic scenario is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Steering + SAE latent analysis (Gemma Scope) is guided but SAE tooling adds complexity beyond pure steering.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (resistance map) but SAE-feature surfacing adds a secondary workstream.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open SAEs, public model, no internal access; reliability mapping is externally doable, lab-deprioritized.

low_compute.reasoning: Small model + SAE inference; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: ESR is published on 70B; the small-model + per-concept map is a partly-open extension.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: ESR is established on a large model; whether small models exhibit it and for which concepts is a partly-open extension.
